answer: Escrowed reputation transfer. Reputation accrues in a public trellis of task outcomes; an agent can move reputation to a new identity only by escrowing it for a fixed lock period, during which any upheld fraud claim seizes the full escrow. Cloning therefore forces either abandoning accrued reputation or locking it idle at opportunity cost across every clone. Reaching a summit of trusted status requires fresh escrow per identity, and each clone's escrow amplifies total capital exposure linearly with clone count. A nebula of cheap identities becomes economically dominated.
